translation_notes: The six next(graph.objects(s, p), 'unknown') calls each become m{ {s} {p} ?v }.first() followed by `if x is None: x = 'unknown'`. next(iterator, default) only substitutes the default on StopIteration (an empty iterator), never on a falsy-but-present value, and an RDF term is never Python None, so `x = default if x is None else x` after .first() is exactly equivalent -- not the shorter `x = m{...}.first() or 'unknown'`, which would (wrongly) also fire on a falsy-but-matched term.

Both subject and predicate are plain Python expressions at every one of the six sites: {node}/{rootentity}/{rootns}/{ns} are the function's own parameters or locals, and the predicate is always an attribute+subscript on self (self.basens['hasNodeId'] etc., a Namespace only known at runtime, not a compile-time prefix), so every site interpolates both terms with {expr} rather than any prefixed name -- there is no @prefix in this file at all.
@graph graph designates the function's own graph parameter as current for the whole body (bound method extracted as a plain function; self is read only for self.basens), so every m{ } stays bare.

Fixture scenarios 1-4 mirror the source repository's own semantic-model/opcua/tests/test_libutils.py::test_generate_node_id (same predicate names, same expected output strings, independently recomputed and checked here): same-namespace with a plain id (prepended), id=None (no prefix), different-namespace (id ignored even though non-empty), and same-namespace with an id that is itself a full IRI (nodeId_to_iri's is_iri branch). Scenario 5 is new here: the zero-solution case, where every one-step read is empty and all six values collapse to 'unknown' on both sides.
